predecessors.name: Kingdom of Spain
predecessors.text: the Spanish monarchy and its possessions

successors.name: Francoist Spain
successors.text: Spain after the Nationalist victory, 1 April 1939

ledger.x: 1931: the Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed on 14 April 1931 (infobox); the page names no territory, so the core is Cliopatria's 1932 shape: Spain with its Moroccan, Saharan and Guinean possessions.
1936: the rising reaches Spanish Morocco on 18 July 1936 and mainland Spain a day later; Spanish Morocco is Nationalist ('control all but certain').
1936: 'Franco and Goded took control of the Canary and Balearic islands to which they were assigned'; the page does not say which Balearic islands (Menorca is not named).

1936: the rising holds Seville, Cadiz, Old Castile, Leon and Galicia while the government keeps Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Malaga, Jaen, Almeria, most of the east coast, Asturias, Cantabria and part of the Basque Country; by October 1936 the rebels held 'much of the south and west' (Second Republic page).
1936: the government moves from Madrid to Valencia on 6 November 1936 as Madrid is under siege.
1937: the Nationalist northern campaign; 'the Nationalists captured most of Spain's northern coastline in 1937' (the page gives no months).
1937: the northern coast is in Nationalist hands by the end of the year (page gives no months).
1937: the north falls to the Nationalists (page: most of the northern coastline captured in 1937; no month for the Basque Country, Santander or Asturias).
1937: the government moves from Valencia to Barcelona on 31 October 1937.
1938: the remaining Nationalist gains between Cliopatria's 1936 and 1938 shapes (Aragon, the push to the Mediterranean, the south-east).
1938: the Nationalist attack on Catalonia; the page says much of Catalonia was captured 'in 1938 and 1939' without dates for the offensive.
1939: Barcelona 'fell to the rebels in early 1939' (Second Republic page; no day).
1939: Catalonia falls; Barcelona 'fell to the rebels in early 1939'.
1939: the Republic 'was dissolved on 1 April 1939' after surrendering in the civil war; its government survived in exile and kept an embassy in Mexico City until 1976.

wars.name: Spanish Civil War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the rising of 17-19 July 1936; Franco enters Madrid and declares victory on 1 April 1939; the Republic is dissolved the same day.

certainty.note: Spain's frontiers and the Moroccan protectorate; the Sahara and Guinea limits are not described on the pages opened.
Front lines; the pages give no monthly line.
